_comment: The gateway mapping for the bind ingress. Same shape as the rate ingress: one
mapping with a route parameter, per-distributor isolation carried by the msr- key.
A distributor's key must allow BOTH /d/<id>/rate and /d/<id>/bind; a key scoped to
one is 401'd on the other, which is the behaviour to want and the one to remember
when a broker reports that quoting works and binding does not.

mapping_version.description: Distribution ingress: broker bind for one distributor

traps: A gateway mapping can be created and patched over HTTP but NEVER removed or disabled: DELETE /gateway/<id>/mapping, PATCH /gateway/<id>/mapping/version and DELETE /gateway/<id>/mapping/version all return 405 on a tenant gateway. Ending a distribution therefore cannot remove its route. Revoking the msr- key is the only de-provisioning lever that works, and it works immediately (measured: 200 before the delete, 401 on the very next request).

quote-bind's BOUND decision carries NO distributor_account_id and NO submission_version, so a projection that trusts the decision is undeliverable for every bind and unorderable if delivered. decision-project resolves both from the submission instead, fetched by id so it cannot race the index.

quote_outcome_config.outcome enumerates ACCEPT/REFER/DECLINE while decision_config.outcome also enumerates BOUND and SANCTION_REFERRAL. Copying the decision's value across 400s the outcome write on every bind; the lifecycle value belongs in outcome_status.

Picking `the newest decision` after a bind is a race: the index flushes on a 1s ticker, so a read taken seconds after quote-bind returns can still hand back the ACCEPT that preceded the BOUND, which then projects REFERRED onto a policy that has just been bound. This flow requires an actual BOUND decision and defers the projection rather than sending the wrong one.
